subject: POC mid‑trial: updated plan, added use cases, and success criteria
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@marketbeat.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap + options to add two extra use cases

Thanks again for taking the call today, Alex — helpful to see how the team is driving the chat+search pilot in production. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we can lock the mid‑trial plan.

Call recap (short):
- Current pilot: chat + product discovery intents (10k monthly queries).
- Business ask: improve routing precision and automate refund amount extraction for escalations.
- Constraint: redacted PII cannot leave MarketBeat systems; latency target <350ms p95.

Suggested mid‑trial changes (we discussed 2 add‑ons):
1) Refund amount extraction: evaluate structured extraction accuracy on 500 labelled threads (sample attached).
2) Cancellation intent routing (edge case coverage): add ~5 intents to the eval set and measure routing F1.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Refund extraction: entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on gold labels.
- Routing: intent classification F1 >= 0.83 across the expanded set.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 350ms on your dev dataset; end‑to‑end pipeline failure rate <1%.

POC owner map and deliverables:
- MarketBeat: provide 500 labelled examples for extraction + 200 chat transcripts for routing by EOD Nov 4.
- Redwood: updated eval harness, updated model variant (quantized) for the trial, daily ingest pipeline for samples, and a revised success matrix.
- Internal owners: Soojin (sales/coord), Karthik (solutions eng), Marissa (CS escalation support).

Timeline (proposed):
- Nov 4: MarketBeat shares labelled samples and security contact.
- Nov 5–8: Redwood runs evals and produces draft results + logs.
- Nov 9: sync to review pass/fail and decide rollforward or fallback.

Attachments: POC_success_matrix_v2.xlsx (scoring thresholds, test sets), sample_convos_marketbeat.csv (anonymized rows).

Ask: Can you confirm the samples timeline and whether MarketBeat wants the refund extraction evaluated on full‑text threads or on the agent summaries? Also confirm whether Security needs to be looped for the ingestion flow.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@marketbeat.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MarketBeat Security <security@marketbeat.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC recap + options to add two extra use cases

Thanks, Soojin — that captures it well. Quick responses inline: 

- Samples: We'll provide 500 labelled refund threads and 250 chat transcripts by COB Nov 4 (we tightened up the labelling ramp). We'll send as anonymized CSVs.
- Extraction scope: run on full thread text first; if that’s blocked by compliance we’ll fall back to agent summaries (we'll flag in the CSV).
- Security: yes — please send the ingestion spec to security@marketbeat.com. They want an outline of what metadata is collected and KMS keys used.

One more ask: can we also evaluate a low‑latency fallback policy where, if the full model exceeds 400ms, we route to a smaller embed+rules flow? That helps our ops team avoid increased SLA violations.

Timeline note: If possible, can Redwood produce preliminary numbers by Nov 7 instead of Nov 8? That would let us review before our Ops sync on Nov 10.

I'll attach a small sample (sample_convos_marketbeat.csv) and the vendor security request form (security_request_form.pdf) in a separate email.

Appreciate it — Alex
Head of Product 
MarketBeat
alex.rivera@marketbeat.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC mid‑trial: updated plan, added use cases, and success criteria

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. We've confirmed internally that we can: 
- Run extraction on full threads and fall back to agent summaries if security prohibits full text.
- Implement a low‑latency fallback policy: we’ll include a smaller quantized model path and a ruleset that executes when p95 model latency > 400ms; we'll surface routing decisions in the logs so you can audit.

Updated plan and commitments (short):
- Nov 4 (by EOD): MarketBeat shares the labelled files + security contact.
- Nov 5–6: Redwood ingests samples, runs nightly evals. We will prioritize delivering a preliminary extraction/confusion matrix by end of day Nov 7 (per your ask).
- Nov 8: Draft results and dashboard (latency/cost breakdowns + test set outcomes).
- Nov 9: Review + decision call to accept scope changes or rollback to original pilot.

Concrete success thresholds we will use in the harness: 
- Refund amount extraction: entity F1 >= 0.88 AND exact match rate >= 0.80 on the labelled set.
- Cancellation routing: macro F1 >= 0.83, per‑intent recall >= 0.78.
- Operational: overall p95 <= 350ms on a 95th‑percentile sample; fallback policy triggers fewer than 3% of requests.

Ownership: Soojin (sales lead / customer coordination), Karthik (SE: ingestion and eval harness + infra), Marissa (CS: success gating and renewal implications).

Notes on price/credits: we'll need to flag this scope change with finance — increased eval compute will incur additional trial credits. If you’d like, I can get a one‑time trial credit estimate and return with a number by Nov 5.

Please reply with a single line confirming the samples timeline and whether Security will accept the ingestion spec via email. Once we have that sign‑off, we'll treat Nov 4 as the gating milestone to run the expanded tests.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
